title: The interaction ledger is built in the P7 functional specification while the ownership ruling and DP-18 give the one ledger to rwb-source-data
source: FSD P7 Decision center and log v3 A1.2 (FEAT-ILG-01 to FEAT-ILG-10) and A2.26 to A2.35; FSD P7 Requirements served (REQ-ILG-001 to REQ-ILG-014); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (no interaction table); Arch v5 slides 20 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling and R5.5 DP-18; Microservice Ownership Map v1 (interaction and efs_ledger_outcome to P1) with ASM-A6-tables-1
section: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 8.1, section 11.2, section 12 OQ-P7-01
description: The P7 functional specification builds the whole interaction ledger in this module: ten features (FEAT-ILG-01 to FEAT-ILG-10) and fourteen program requirements (REQ-ILG-001 to REQ-ILG-014) sit in P7, with the ledger table, the ordered read and the deduplication rule all described here. The R-PREC default ruling gives the interaction ledger to rwb-source-data and DP-18 repeats it, the Ownership Map records interaction and efs_ledger_outcome as P1's with that reason, and the P1 PRD already carries the capability as CAP-P1-012 with FR-P1-029 and FR-P1-030. Two modules cannot both own the authoritative case history: the ledger table, the write path, the deduplication and the ordered read would be built twice or not at all, and the case timeline in P3 would read one of two answers.
evidence: FSD P7 A1.2 lists FEAT-ILG-01 to FEAT-ILG-10 as P7 features and A2.26 to A2.35 build the ledger table, the ordered read and the duplicate rule; the Ownership Map ruling reads 'Ledger and intake rule stay with P1 rwb-source-data (R-PREC default ruling, DP-18); the case timeline and interaction API stay with P3'; Template and Rules R3 fixes 'Interaction ledger | P1 rwb-source-data'; the P1 PRD carries CAP-P1-012.
area: rwb-decision scope, the interaction ledger and the case history
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data and rwb-case contract owners
proposed: Confirm at the wave 1 contract review that rwb-source-data owns the one ledger (table, write, deduplication, ordered read and retention class) and that rwb-case serves the timeline over its contract; re-issue FSD P7 without FEAT-ILG-01 to FEAT-ILG-10 and without A2.26 to A2.35, and keep REQ-ILG-001 to REQ-ILG-014 traced to CAP-P1-012. Until then this PRD keeps only the decision ledger and lists the ledger as a dependency.

title: The daily copy of the decision log to the data lake and its row-count reconciliation have no target under Architecture v5
source: FSD P7 v3 FEAT-DRI-06 (A2.6) and AC-P7-006-01 to AC-EXC-P7-006-04; BRD Program v4 REQ-DRI-009; TSD P7 v2 T5.1 (INT-19, INT-20); Arch v5 slides 20, 28, 37 and 44 (JOB-13 continuous ingest); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17
section: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 9, section 11.2, section 12 OQ-P7-02
description: REQ-DRI-009 requires the decision log to be copied to the data lake daily with row counts matched, and the FSD builds that copy as FEAT-DRI-06 with JOB-13 at 01:00, a watermark, a manifest and check REC-08. Architecture v5 removes the data lake (ADR-018): reporting reads events into rwb-reporting, JOB-13 keeps its ID with 'ingest is continuous (Kafka)', and DP-17 records the lake as removed. The requirement therefore has no target and no consumer, and its acceptance criteria describe a store that will not exist. A PRD that kept it would create a backlog item for removed infrastructure.
evidence: FSD P7 A2.6 AC-P7-006-01 reads 'the data lake copy has the same row count and the same last hash as the live log'; TSD P7 T5.1 lists INT-19 'Data lake and Power BI' and INT-20; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-13 reads 'Decision log copy | 01:00 | rwb-decision | ingest is continuous (Kafka)'; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17 reads 'Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting'.
owner_role: Solution architect with the reporting and BI analyst
proposed: Retire REQ-DRI-009 with RWB-E1-014 (already recorded as retired in the Change Register) and re-issue FSD P7 without FEAT-DRI-06 and its acceptance criteria; record in the P9 PRD that reporting reads DecisionRecorded into its own read model, and keep the population query of this service as the audit path.

title: Notice generation, letter templates, the template catalog and proof of delivery are built in P7 while the ownership ruling gives notices and templates to rwb-comms
source: FSD P7 v3 A2.10 to A2.13 (FEAT-DRI-14 to FEAT-DRI-17); TSD P7 v2 T5.2 and T5.1; Arch v5 slide 41 (P6 owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery) and slide 19 (P6 OUT); Microservice Ownership Map v1 (notice and template to P6); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-16
section: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 9, section 11.2, section 12 OQ-P7-03
description: The P7 functional specification builds four features that belong to the communications service: generating demand, recall and guarantor notices into WIN, managing letter templates with Legal approval, holding the template catalog with its merge fields, and capturing proof of delivery from WIN. The Ownership Map records notice and template as P6's, Architecture v5 gives rwb-comms the notice pipeline and the WIN file through rwb-integration, and the API and error messages used by those criteria (MSG-P6-003, MSG-P6-005, MSG-P6-007) are already the communications service's. P7 keeps only the approval of a D7.1 notice, which is the first use of approval routing and is REQ-APD-006.
evidence: FSD P7 A1.2 rows FEAT-DRI-14 to FEAT-DRI-17 are kind 'System' or 'Admin' in P7, and AC-P7-010-01 to AC-EXC-P7-013-08 build the notice, the template version and the WIN acknowledgement; Architecture v5 slide 41 gives P6 'notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery'; the Ownership Map lists notice and template under P6.
area: rwb-decision scope, notice generation and templates
owner_role: Business lead with Legal counsel and the rwb-comms owner
proposed: Move FEAT-DRI-14 to FEAT-DRI-17 and A2.10 to A2.13 with their acceptance criteria to the rwb-comms and rwb-document documents, keep FEAT-APD-08 and AC-P7-022-01 to AC-EXC-P7-022-04 here as the notice approval, and correct TSD P7 T5.2 so that the notice is reached through the rwb-comms contract.

title: The rule registry, its four tables and its version operations are claimed by three documents and owned by one service
source: TSD P7 v2 T1, T2 and T3.1 (no rule tables or rule operations); TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T-A.1 API-P4-014 to API-P4-020; TSD P3 v3 appendix T-A API-P3-020 to API-P3-026; API Specification v4 x-module P3 and v3 x-module P4; Arch v5 slides 14, 27 and 41; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 15; Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling with ASM-A6-tables-3 and ASM-A6-api-3
section: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 6 FR-P7-030 to FR-P7-033, section 9, section 12 OQ-P7-04
description: Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-decision the DMN model registry, slide 27 makes rule governance central here, and the R-PREC default ruling gives the rule package registry to P7 with the four tables. The P3 and P4 technical specifications both declare rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case and both claim the load, approve, rollback, dry-run and change-report operations, and the API Specification v4 marks the paths x-module P3 while v3 marked them P4. The P7 technical specification has none of them, so the service that is meant to own the registry has no field list and no operation inventory for it, while two other services have both.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 41 row P7 reads 'approvals, central decision ledger, DMN model registry'; slide 27 reads 'GOVERNED CENTRALLY - rule registry in rwb-decision (P7)'; the Ownership Map ruling reads 'Rule registry, rule rows and rule test cases stay with P7 rwb-decision ... services hold only a local evaluated copy (DP-04), despite TSD P4 v3 and TSD P3 v3 declaring these tables'; TSD P7 T3.1 lists only decision_log_entry and approval.
area: rwb-decision rule registry, its tables and its operations
legacy_ref: RWB-E1-029; RWB-E1-072; RWB-E1-073; RWB-E2-041; RWB-E2-042; RWB-AD-011; RWB-AD-012; RWB-AD-013
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform contract owner
proposed: Re-issue TSD P7 with T3.1 entries for the four rule tables and with appendix T-A carrying the rule-version and rule-package operations, remove those tables and operations from TSD P3 and TSD P4, and correct the x-module of the nine rule paths in the API Specification to P7. Until then this PRD states the registry as this service's and the operations as its contract, with OQ-P7-04 open.

title: The delegation of authority table is loaded and approved inside P7 while the ownership ruling gives the table to rwb-access
source: FSD P7 v3 A2.24 AC-P7-024-01 to AC-EXC-P7-024-05 and TSD P7 v2 T3.3 (delegation_limit relationship); Arch v5 slide 14 (P7 OUT 'REST Access: DoA limits'); Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling (delegation_limit to P4) with ASM-A6-tables-4
section: Section 2.3, section 5.1, section 9, section 9.1, section 12 OQ-P7-05
description: A2.24 loads the delegation of authority file from the regulation into the table, approves it, refuses a falling limit or an unknown decision code and rolls a version back, and the P7 technical specification holds a relationship from approval to delegation_limit. Architecture v5 slide 14 gives P7 only 'REST Access: DoA limits' on the outbound side, and the Ownership Map rules the DoA table to rwb-access with the reason that the versioned reference-data wording does not move it. The decision content and the limit lookup belong to this service; the table, its load and its approval belong to the access service, and the refusal messages (MSG-P1-002, MSG-P7-002, MSG-P4-002) belong to whichever service validates the file.
evidence: FSD P7 AC-P7-024-01 reads '218 rows are stored ... and no two rows repeat the same decision, regulation item, product, level and limits'; TSD P7 T3.3 relates approval to delegation_limit; Arch v5 slide 14 P7 OUT reads 'REST Access: DoA limits'; the Ownership Map ruling reads 'The DoA table is P4 rwb-access (Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 v3)'.
area: delegation of authority, limit lookup and approval routing
owner_role: Risk and model risk officer with the rwb-access owner
proposed: Keep in this service only the lookup at the moment of the decision and the recording of the row ID and version; move A2.24 with AC-P7-024-01 to AC-EXC-P7-024-05 to rwb-access, and confirm the lookup answer shape (level, row ID, version, NOT_COVERED, RELATED_PARTY reason) in the access contract. Until then this PRD reads the limits and records the version, and OQ-P7-05 stays open.

title: The ledger completeness target, the gap alert threshold and the strict-mode wait bound have no value in the BRD or the FSD
source: Arch v5 slides 20 and 28 (five minutes, gap alerts, chain verification); FSD P7 v3 A2.5 and A2.25 (no numeric target); BRD Program v4 NFR-033 to NFR-035 (no numeric target); TSD P7 v2 T7 (no completeness entry)
section: Section 6 FR-P7-009, section 9.1, section 11.1 AC-P7-005, section 12 OQ-P7-06
description: Architecture v5 states that rwb-decision reads the decision-record topic into the ledger within five minutes, raises gap alerts and verifies the chain, and that strict mode waits for the ledger acknowledgement at four points of no return. Neither the BRD's auditability requirements nor the FSD gives a completeness target, an alert threshold or a bound on the strict-mode wait, and the technical specification does not carry one either. Without a value the ingest cannot be sized, the alert cannot be tested and a caller cannot say how long a point of no return may wait.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 28 note reads 'rwb-decision consumes it idempotently into the central ledger, with a 5-minute completeness target, gap alerts and chain verification'; the same slide says strict mode steps 'wait until the central ledger confirms the record' with no bound; BRD NFR-033 to NFR-035 state reproducibility, the rule version and the daily check only.
area: decision-record ingest service level and strict mode
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform administrator
proposed: Set the completeness target, the gap alert threshold and the maximum strict-mode wait as one reference-data row each, proposed as the five minutes of Architecture v5 for the target and the alert, and confirm the wait bound with Risk and Internal Audit at the ADR-022 sign-off.

title: The decision log and the ledger carry no retention period, and the WORM seal period is unstated
source: BRD Program v4 NFR-030 and NFR-075 (open under DL26); FSD P7 v3 A2.1 and A2.27 (no period); Arch v5 slide 28 (daily seal, no period); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (no retention column)
description: NFR-030 leaves the decision-log retention to Compliance with no period and NFR-075 does the same for the interaction ledger, both under DL26. The FSD requires the ledger to be held for the period the regulator and internal audit require and the FSD gives the ledger its own class, but no table carries a retention class or a period, and the WORM seal has no stated life. The class can be declared and enforced, but the age at which an entry may be disposed of, and the age of a seal, cannot be tested.
evidence: BRD Program v4 NFR-030 reads 'The decision log is retained for the period the regulator and internal audit require. | Log retention is set by Compliance | Open, DL26'; NFR-075 reads 'Interaction ledger entries carry their own retention period, set independently of the decision log. | Not set | Open, DL26'; TSD P7 T3.1 has no retention field.
area: retention and evidence life of the decision ledger
proposed: Set the decision-log class period and the seal period under DL26 before the first release, keep the class per record class in reference data, and state in the retention rule that no archive runs inside this service.

title: A committee decision has no field for the members present or their votes, although the requirement and the screen need both
source: BRD Program v4 REQ-APD-008; FSD P7 v3 Screens (SCR-12 Committee pack, first in E4) and A2.16 committee path; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 approval field list (no member or vote field)
section: Section 5 CAP-P7-014, section 6 FR-P7-025, section 11.1 AC-P7-017, section 12 OQ-P7-08
description: REQ-APD-008 requires a committee decision to be recorded against the item with the members present and the decision taken, and SCR-12 shows each member's vote. The approval field list has a single approver, a level, a status and a terms document, and no member, no vote and no quorum; the decision-log entry has one approver and one final call. Recording the committee in the terms document is possible but unqueryable, which defeats the audit request that the requirement exists for.
evidence: REQ-APD-008 reads 'A committee decision is recorded against the item with the members present and the decision taken.'; FSD P7 Screens row SCR-12 reads 'The pack for a committee decision with each member's vote', first in E4; TSD P7 T3.1 approval ends at DF-DEC-053 decision_log_id with no member or vote field.
owner_role: Business lead with the center of excellence analyst
proposed: Agree a member and vote structure for the committee path before Epic 4, either as two child tables of approval or as a versioned structure inside terms, and extend the decision-log entry so the committee's outcome and its members are queryable in the population query.

title: The rule model format is XLS decision tables today and DMN 1.6 in the target, with no ruling on which the registry accepts
source: Arch v5 slides 27 and 33 (OMG DMN 1.6 proposal, conformance level 3); Temporal and Drools Design v1 T4 (XLS workbook compiled to a KieBase) and its open points; ADR-012 and ADR-017; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (no rule table)
description: Architecture v5 proposes moving the rule packages to OMG DMN 1.6 decision models, table by table, on the same Drools runtime, while the Temporal and Drools design describes today's XLS decision-table workbook compiled to a KieBase with at least 50 scenarios. ADR-012 keeps XLS and ADR-017 sets the governance model, and neither fixes which format the registry accepts at go-live, nor whether a package may exist in both. The load checks, the checksum and the model fetch differ between the two formats, so the registry contract cannot be closed without the answer.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 27 notes read 'Today (ADR-012): embedded Drools with XLS decision tables ... Proposal: OMG DMN 1.6 decision models ... both run on the same Drools runtime, so tables are converted one at a time with no big bang'; Temporal and Drools Design T4 reads 'RW-COE writes each rule package as an Excel workbook in Drools XLS decision-table format'.
owner_role: Center of excellence analyst with the solution architect
proposed: Record in ADR-017 that the registry accepts an XLS decision table and a DMN 1.6 model as two package formats on one runtime, that a package version names its format, and that the conversion is a version change with its own test evidence; keep both formats in the load checks and the model fetch.

title: Four screens are attributed to P7 while the edge ruling composes every screen in gateway-bff
source: FSD P7 v3 Screens (SCR-10, SCR-11, SCR-12, SCR-38); Arch v5 slides 19 and 41 (gateway-bff, one hop); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19; TSD P7 v2 appendix T-A (operations only)
description: The P7 functional specification attributes SCR-10 Approval queue, SCR-11 Decision screen, SCR-12 Committee pack and SCR-38 Decision log query to this module, while DP-19 and the edge ruling put every screen behind gateway-bff, built against the service contracts and the platform screen pattern. The technical specification lists only REST operations and no screen inventory, so nothing says who builds the four screens or which of them is a composite of this service and rwb-case. The wave 2 slice cannot be estimated until the split is fixed.
evidence: FSD P7 Screens lists SCR-10 'first in E2', SCR-11 'first in E2', SCR-12 'first in E4' and SCR-38 'first in E2'; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-19 reads 'Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route'; TSD P7 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P7-001 to API-P7-008 and no screen.
owner_role: Solution architect with the platform edge owner
proposed: Fix in the edge and gateway design which of the four screens gateway-bff composes from this service's operations and which states the service owns (queue item, decision detail, committee pack, search result), and record the four screen contracts there rather than in this PRD.

title: The decision record is published by 19 services on one topic with no schema version field in the field list
source: Arch v5 slides 28 and 42 (EV-08 on rwb.decision-record.v1, producer all 19); TSD P7 v2 T3.1 decision_log_entry field list (no schema version); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09 (CloudEvents) and DP-14
section: Section 6 FR-P7-001, section 9, section 9.1, section 12 OQ-P7-11
description: Nineteen services publish DecisionRecorded on one shared topic and this service consumes it into a single ledger. The field list of decision_log_entry has no schema version and no producer version, and the CloudEvents envelope carries a type and a source but no contract version. A field added by one producer, or a rule version whose format changes, would reach the consumer with no way to tell which contract the producer used, and the ledger would hold mixed shapes without saying so.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 reads 'DecisionRecorded | all 19 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | rwb-decision, rwb-reporting'; TSD P7 T3.1 lists DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031 with no schema or producer version; DP-09 sets CloudEvents for every event.
proposed: Add a contract version to the DecisionRecorded event in the event and messaging design, record it on the ledger entry, and let the consumer accept a known set of versions and send an unknown one to the dead-letter topic rather than guessing.

title: The Waiting approval case state and the approval task are set inside P7 while the case state and the queue belong to rwb-case
source: FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-015-01 ('the case status becomes Waiting approval'), A2.16 step 3 and A2.23; Arch v5 slides 14 and 41 (rwb-case owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks); Microservice Ownership Map v1 (case, task and queue to P3)
description: The approval criteria require the case status to become Waiting approval when an approval is routed, and the FSD describes the service raising a task where a person is needed. The case state machine, the queues and the tasks are rwb-case's under Architecture v5 and the ownership map, and this service writes only rwb_decision. Either this service calls the case contract to move the state and raise the task, or P3 moves the state on ApprovalRequested; the PRD cannot state one and the backlog cannot estimate the approval slice until it is fixed.
evidence: FSD P7 AC-P7-015-01 ends 'And the case status becomes "Waiting approval"'; Arch v5 slide 41 gives rwb-case 'case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers'; the Ownership Map lists case and task under P3; TSD P7 T4 reads 'No case state machine of its own'.
area: approval routing, case state and tasks
owner_role: Solution architect with the rwb-case contract owner
proposed: Decide in the case contract whether the state move and the task are a P3 reaction to ApprovalRequested (preferred, one writer of the case state) or a P3 operation this service calls in the same step; record the choice in the contract and in the FSD acceptance criteria of A2.15 and A2.16.
